newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Starfish hold secret of N.Sea pollution - scientists.
newsitem.headline: Starfish hold secret of N.Sea pollution - scientists.

text.p: Starfish may hold the secret to monitoring pollution in the North Sea, a team of Belgian scientists claimed on Thursday.
The marine biologists from Brussels Free University (ULB) have discovered the common sea creatures retain pollutants like lead and cadmium in their skeletons, sometimes for years.
"The ULB team will use this new bio-indicator in a large scale trial to monitor the (river) Schelde estuary and Belgian coast later this year," Dr Ali Temara told Reuters.
He said the trial would extend as far into the North Sea as the Dogger Bank.
The team has already tested the technique in Norway with help from researchers at the Norwegian Institute of Aquatic Studies (NIVA).
Together the scientists used starfish to measure the presence of heavy metals in Sorgford, near Odda, which is known to be polluted as a result of nearby zinc smelting, Temara said.
"It turned out that the results from the starfish better reflected the quality of the environment than mussels, the other organism commonly used to survey marine pollution," he said.
Temara said the team's results had already been published in several specialised scientific journals and further publications were pending.
